By means of the instant writ petition, the petitioners seek to challenge the order dated 24.02.2023 passed by the Additional District Magistrate (Prescribed Authority) Land Acquisition, Jaunpur,
whereby while allowing the recall/restoration application dated 26.08.2022, filed by the complainant namely respondent No.5, the order dated 05.07.2022 for disbursement of compensation to the petitioners has been recalled.

sentences.text: The award in the name of the petitioners for Arazi No.80 has been cancelled and direction has been given to them to refund the compensation already paid to them.

It is sought to be submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the order impugned is hit by Section 3-H(4) of the National Highways Act, 1956, inasmuch as, in case of any dispute Shree Gullu And Another vs Union Of India And 4 Others on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62677894/

sentences.text: pertaining to apportionment of compensation, it was incumbent upon the competent authority to refer the matter/dispute to the competent Civil Court.
It is, thus, argued that the respondent No.3 has committed illegality in passing the order impugned and asking the petitioners to refund the compensation disbursed to them.

Considering this submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners, we have gone through the order impugned which records that the plot No.80 is a big plot and in a portion of the said plot,
NH-56 has been constructed.

After making an inquiry into the matter of utilisation of portion of Gata No.80, compensation has been paid to the tenure holders of the portion which has been utilised for construction of National Highway.

On the complaint made by the respondent No.5, it is noted in the order impugned that in Gata No.80, the interest of the State is involved, and the portion of Gata No.80 which is in possession of the petitioners is lying much away from the road constructed as NH-56.

The attention of the Court is invited to the map incorporated in the order impugned to demonstrate that the portion of Gata No.80 (which is a big plot), which is in occupation of the petitioners, is much away from NH-56.

A categorical finding has been returned in the order impugned that portion of Gata No.80, which is in occupation of the petitioners, has not been acquired and, thus, there was no question of payment of compensation to them.

On a pointed query made by the Court as to whether the names of the petitioners are recorded in the revenue records with respect to Gata No.80, a copy of Khatauni for Fasli Year 1426-31 has been placed before us wherein the names of the petitioners have been recorded in Gata No.80 in an area of 0.0570 hectares.
The total area of Gata No.80 is not on record.
From a perusal of the averments of the order impugned, it seems that there are several tenure holders of Gata No.80 and some portion of the said plot has also been recorded as Navin Parti.

In the said scenario, in absence of clear position with regard to acquisition of Gata No.80 area 0.0570 hectares belonging to the petitioners for construction of NH-56, we do not find any error in the order of the competent authority namely A.D.M. (Land Acquisition), Jaunpur in setting aside the order dated 05.07.2022 for disbursement of compensation to the petitioners.

However, it is open for the petitioners to approach the competent revenue authority by invoking the provisions of U.P. Revenue Code, 2006 for identification/demarcation of the portion of Gata No.80 to ascertain the extent of lands acquired for construction of NH-56.
The question of payment of compensation to the petitioners would be subject to the decision of the revenue authority.
In any case, no interference is called for in the order impugned.
The writ petition is, thus, dismissed.
It is made clear that the revenue authority shall be under obligation to decide the matter independently without being influenced by any of the observations made herein above.
The dismissal of the instant petition shall not come in the way of the petitioners in such decision.
